prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage. Bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design.
2. One dominant flat block-colour background for the whole shot: lime green. Never a rainbow, never a gradient.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Never a recognisable person's face.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the background's contrasting colour. Real paper texture, print dots, small tape pieces.
5. Consistent upper-left light. Small paper-layer shadows only.
6. Everything is flat matte printed paper. No glow, no neon, no bloom, no halos, no luminous edges. Nothing emits light. Not glossy 3D. Not live action.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif, black or cream, printed on paper chips, large, safe margins. English spelling and letterforms accurate and stable. Only the headline text in the copy list, nothing else.
8. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window. One strongest visual focus at a time. No camera shake. Movement starts on the first frame; a small loop continues at the end. No empty frames.
9. Numbers, when specified, are printed complete from their first visible frame. Never counting up, never morphing, never redrawn.
10. No brands, logos, watermarks, or text beyond the copy list.
11. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
12. Identity anchor: rough white torn-paper edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: lime green.
Subjects: the ribbon; a paper map shape.
Opens on the ribbon, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The ribbon loops around a cutout map shape that lifts and holds centre frame.
Ends holding on the map shape.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "$77B MARKET".

COPY LIST: "$77B MARKET". Exact strings; nothing else appears in frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "Diginex has signalled focus on Brazil's seventy-seven billion dollar sustainability market as a new revenue stream.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage in a 2D motion design style. The scene opens on <Picture 1>, featuring a flat, matte lime green background with a consistent light source from the upper-left casting small, soft shadows beneath the paper elements. A cream-colored matte paper ribbon, carried over from the previous sequence, is positioned in the center. Simultaneously, a black-and-white halftone photographic cutout of a map shape, characterized by rough white torn-paper edges and a grainy print texture, enters the frame quickly from the bottom with a slight overshoot before stabilizing in the center. The cream ribbon fluidly loops around the map cutout as it lifts into its central position. A rectangular paper chip in cream enters the frame with a fast, snappy motion, bearing the headline "$77B MARKET" in a large, extra-bold black sans-serif typeface; the text is clean, legible, and stable. As the action settles, the map shape and ribbon maintain a subtle, slow-pulsing loop of movement. Throughout the shot, the camera remains a Static Shot. A narrator (S1), a male with a warm, clear, and natural timbre and a brisk but unhurried speaking rate, says: <d>[English] Diginex has signalled focus on Brazil's seventy-seven billion dollar sustainability market as a new revenue stream.</d>

overall_soundscape: The audio is dominated by the narrator's voice, layered with tactile foley sounds. This includes the crisp, percussive slap of heavy paper hitting a surface and the sticky, short rip of adhesive tape being applied, synchronized with the arrival of the map and the headline chip.
